title: Austin Energy, Aid, and Infrastructure
summary:
*   Approved funding to kickstart new alternative energy projects for the city.
*   Allocated federal oil overcharge refunds to the "Plus + 1" Program, providing assistance for needy electric utility customers.
*   Authorized the purchase of a new aerial tower truck for the Electric Utility Department, a significant capital investment.
*   Postponed the selection of a site for a future energy control center, signaling upcoming decisions on critical energy infrastructure.

MEETING AS THE ELECTRIC UTILITY BOARD
Council Chambers, 307 West Second Street, Austin, Texas Mayor Cooke called to order the
meeting of the Council, noting the absence of Councilmember Urdy.
The report of the Electric Utility Commission was heard. CONSENT ORDINANCES The Council,
on Mayor Pro Tem Shipman's motion, Councilmember Carl-Mitchell's second, waived the
requirment for three readings and finally passed the following ordinances in one motion:
(6-0 Vote, Councilmember Urdy absent)
Alternative Energy Projects
Accepted funds from the State of Texas in the amount of $48,850.00 and amend the Capital
Improvement Program by appropriating this money to the Electric Utility Department for
three alternative energy projects.
"Plus + 1" Program
Accepted an oil overcharge refund from the U.S. Department of Energy in the amount of
$24,004.00 and amend the 1988-89 Annual Operating Budget by appropriating this money to
the "Plus + 1" Program to assist needy electric utility customers. CONSENT RESOLUTIONS The
Council, on Mayor Pro Tem Shipman's motion, Councilmember Humphrey's second, adopted the

Authorized the City Manager or her designee to enter into a contract between the City of
Austin/LCRA and Sun Coal Company for a three month supply of coal (10/1/89-12/31/89) for
the Fayette Power Project. Total estimated cost is $501,494 with the City of Austin share
at $250,747.
Pipeline Easement
Granted Clajon Gas Company a pipeline easement across the Fayette Power Project for the
purpose of collecting the gas production from the recently drilled Norman #31 gas well at
the Project. (City will receive $1,229.10)
